posts.title: KVM Page Eviction, Part 2: Tracking Page Use
posts.description: In Part 1 , we replaced FIFO with CLOCK in KVM’s legacy memory management unit (MMU) for a UCSD class project. KVM caches address mappings in shadow pages . Evicting a shadow page discards those mappings while leaving guest memory intact. If the guest accesses that memory again, a page fault lets KVM rebuild the missing mapping. FIFO evicts the oldest shadow pages first. CLOCK skips a shadow page

posts.title: opthash: Bridging Theory with Hardware
posts.description: Earlier this year, a Quanta video on 2025’s biggest breakthroughs in computer science showcased a result about hash tables that motivated me to implement it. The paper, Optimal Bounds for Open Addressing Without Reordering , presents Elastic Hashing and Funnel Hashing: two ways to keep insertion and successful lookup cheap even when a table is nearly full, without moving entries after placing them
